steps.title: A crystal is an order
steps.text: In a crystal, the atoms are arranged in a pattern that repeats in space, like bricks in a wall. This pattern is described by three axes (a, b, c) and the three angles between them (α, β, γ). Depending on the lengths of the axes and on the angles, there are only seven crystal systems.

steps.title: Cubic system
steps.text: Form: three equal axes, perpendicular to each other. Symmetry: the highest: 3 four-fold axes, 4 three-fold axes. Habit: cubes, octahedra, dodecahedra. Stones: diamond, garnets, spinel, fluorite. Optics: isotropic, a single refraction.

steps.title: Tetragonal system
steps.text: Form: two equal axes, a third one different, all perpendicular. Symmetry: one four-fold axis. Habit: prisms with a square base, bipyramids. Stones: zircon, rutile, vesuvianite. Optics: uniaxial.

steps.title: Hexagonal system
steps.text: Form: three equal axes in one plane, at 120° from each other, and a perpendicular vertical axis. Symmetry: one six-fold axis. Habit: six-sided prisms. Stones: beryl (emerald, aquamarine), apatite. Optics: uniaxial.

steps.title: Trigonal system
steps.text: Form: close to hexagonal, but with a three-fold axis only (it is also described by a rhombohedron: three equal axes, tilted the same way). Habit: three- or six-sided prisms, rhombohedra, terminations. Stones: quartz (amethyst, citrine), corundum (ruby, sapphire), tourmaline, calcite. Optics: uniaxial.

steps.title: Orthorhombic system
steps.text: Form: three axes of different lengths, all perpendicular. Symmetry: three two-fold axes. Habit: prisms with a diamond-shaped base, tabular crystals. Stones: topaz, peridot, chrysoberyl, tanzanite, andalusite. Optics: biaxial.

steps.title: Monoclinic system
steps.text: Form: three unequal axes, one of which is tilted: only one angle differs from 90°. Symmetry: a single two-fold axis. Habit: flattened prisms, twinned crystals. Stones: jadeite, orthoclase, spodumene (kunzite), malachite. Optics: biaxial.

steps.title: Triclinic system
steps.text: Form: three unequal axes, no right angle. Symmetry: the lowest: at best a centre of symmetry. Habit: irregular crystals, plates. Stones: feldspars (amazonite, labradorite), turquoise, rhodonite. Optics: biaxial.

steps.title: Growth axes and habit
steps.text: A crystal does not grow the same way in all directions: it grows faster along some axes. If growth is fast along c, you get a needle; if it is fast along a and b, a plate. This outer shape is the habit. Above all, properties change with direction: refractive index, colour (pleochroism), hardness. This is why the stone is turned under the instruments, and why the lapidary orients it to get the finest colour.
